summary: Robert B. Ekvall (1898–1983) worked in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He was a research associate at the University of Chicago (~1953–1957), a research fellow and chairman at the University of Washington (1958), and honorary curator at the Burke Museum (~1975–1983).

Robert Baker Aitken (1917–2010) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi, UC Berkeley, Ryutaku-ji, and under numerous Zen teachers. He held posts at Besant Hill School, East-West Center, and University of Hawaiʻi.

Robert Barnett (born 1953) is a Tibetology scholar educated at the University of Cambridge (~1973–1976). He served as an adjunct professor at Columbia University (~1999–2018), directed Tibet University's summer program (2000–2006), and held posts at SOAS and King's College London.

Robert Caesar Childers (1838–1876) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Wadham College, Oxford (~1856–1860) and under Yātrāmullē Dhammārāma (~1863–1864), later serving at the India Office (1872) and as professor at University College London (~1872–1876).

Robert Chalmers (1858–1938) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oriel College, Oxford, and under T. W. Rhys Davids. He served as president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1922–1925) and Master of Peterhouse (1924–1931).

Robert Chambers (1737–1803) was a legal scholar and Indologist who studied at Lincoln College, Oxford. He served as Vinerian Professor of English Law at Oxford (1766), Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Fort William (~1789–1798), and Asiatic Society president (~1797–1798).

Robert Charles Zaehner (1913–1974) studied at Christ Church, Oxford, and under Harold Walter Bailey at Cambridge. A scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Iranian studies, he served as Oxford's Professor of Eastern Religions and Ethics and All Souls fellow (1952–1974).

Robert DeCaroli (born 1970) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and art history who completed his MA and PhD at UCLA under Robert L. Brown and Katherine Anne Harper. He joined the George Mason University faculty around 2000.

Robert Deliège (born 1953) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Oxford (~1980–1983) and held posts at the University of Kerala and UCLouvain, where he became a professor around 1989.
Robert Duquenne is a Buddhist studies scholar who worked as a specialist in Tantric Buddhism at Hōbōgirin (attested 1981) and held a post at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2009).

Robert E. Buswell Jr. (born 1953) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kusan Sunim and completed his AB, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley under Lewis Lancaster and others. He was a professor at UCLA (~1994–2022).

Robert E. Morrell specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Robert H. Brower and William H. McCullough, and held a post at Washington University in St. Louis (attested 1985 and 2006).

Robert E. Svoboda (born 1953) specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Oklahoma (~1970–1972) and under Vimalananda (~1975–1983), later holding adjunct posts at Bastyr University and The Ayurvedic Institute (attested 2008).

Robert F. Rhodes is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Harvard University. He served as a professor at Otani University (attested 1993–1997 and 2012–2014) and committee member of the Otani Academic Society (attested 2000).

Robert Florida works in religious and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University and was an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).
Robert Ford Campany (born 1959) is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He was a professor at Indiana University (~1989–2004) and later joined Vanderbilt University (~2010).

Robert Gardner (1925–2014) earned his BA at Harvard University (~1943–1947), worked at the Fogg Museum (~1947–1949), and taught at the University of Puget Sound before serving as a professor at Harvard University (1956–1997).

Robert Gauthiot (1876–1916) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He was educated at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and was a member of the Société Asiatique from 1909.

Robert Göbl (1919–1997) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna (1947–1950) and later held an academic post there from around 1955 to 1989.

Robert H. Brower (1923–1988) was a Japanologist who earned degrees at Harvard (~1941–1944) and Michigan (~1945–1947). He taught at Minnesota (1951–1954) and Stanford (1954–1966), before chairing Far Eastern Languages and Literatures at Michigan (1966–1988).
